items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I played with him with Maynard.

ctx.x: What lead player do you admire the most?

Trombone players? It was Bobby Burgess. Bobby Burgess was with Stan Kenton, and then he was with Maynard. I played with him with Maynard. He was very consistent. There are guys that play higher than him, but there are not guys that are more consistent than he was.
Bill – let’s maybe segue to the most recent – there have been only two World of Trombone projects?

items.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: when we did the trombone thing recently at the Blue Note with Bobby Burgess and Bill Watrous you know, those guys and Benny Powell, they love to work together

ctx.x: To get a rehearsal in and scheduling.

It’s a job. When we did the trombone album, the trombone CD, we did that one thing, but we could never have that same group again. But we had good guys after that too, guys that weren’t on the CD. And when we did the trombone thing recently at the Blue Note with Bobby Burgess and Bill Watrous you know, those guys and Benny Powell, they love to work together so they’ll just about do anything they can to get to work in that group
because they loved being there so much. But in general when you’ve got a group like that it’s hard to get that group together more than once. There always will be some change in there.
